channel.title: WalkFirst Blog
channel.description: The WalkFirst blog: research-backed posts on walking, daily steps, screen time and habits, from the developer of the WalkFirst app.

item.title: A 4-week walking plan for beginners: from 10 minutes to 150 a week
item.description: Start with 10 minutes a day and build to the 150 minutes a week health guidelines recommend. A simple 4-week walking plan, with pace and habit tips.

item.title: Walking after eating: does a 10-minute walk lower blood sugar?
item.description: A short walk after meals blunts the blood sugar spike. What the studies found, why timing matters, and how to make a 10-minute walk after dinner a habit.

item.title: Does walking count as exercise? How much you need each week
item.description: Brisk walking counts as moderate exercise. How fast "brisk" is, the 150 minutes a week adults need, and whether short walks add up.

item.title: How to block Instagram on iPhone — every method, honestly ranked
item.description: Screen Time limits, Downtime, deleting the app, and third-party blockers — every way to block Instagram on iPhone, ranked by how hard it is to bypass.

item.title: Friction is the only habit hack that ever worked for me
item.description: Motivation fades and discipline runs out. Redesigning the friction around your habits — making bad ones harder and good ones easier — is what actually lasts.

item.title: A morning routine you'll actually keep has only three pieces
item.description: Forget the 5am club and the 12-step rituals. A durable morning routine has three pieces: water, light, and movement — in any order, at any hour.

item.title: Checking your phone in bed is ruining your morning — here's the fix
item.description: Why the first ten minutes of phone use set your whole day's attention pattern, and a three-tier fix from gentle to bulletproof.

item.title: How many steps a day do you really need? It depends on your goal
item.description: Longevity, weight, mood, or just getting started — the right daily step goal is different for each. Here are the honest numbers per goal.

item.title: Doomscrolling: why your brain can't stop — and the fix that isn't willpower
item.description: Doomscrolling isn't a discipline problem — it's a design problem. Here's the psychology behind the loop and the friction-based fix that actually works.

item.title: A realistic healthy daily schedule for people with desk jobs
item.description: No 5am club, no two-hour routines — a sustainable daily structure for desk workers built around movement, light, and a phone that knows its place.

item.title: How much screen time is too much? An honest answer
item.description: There's no magic number of hours. Here's the honest way to judge your screen time — three questions that matter more than any average.

item.title: What 30 minutes of walking a day actually changes
item.description: The realistic benefits of a daily 30-minute walk — mood, sleep, blood pressure, creativity — from someone who builds walking software for a living.

item.title: Is 10,000 steps a myth? What the science actually says
item.description: 10,000 steps started as pedometer marketing, not medicine. Here's what step-count research really shows, and how to pick a goal that fits you.

item.title: Introducing WalkFirst: your steps are the key to your apps
item.description: Why I built an app that blocks distracting apps until you've walked enough — and how Apple's Screen Time framework makes it possible fully on-device.
